one-thing.title: Yon comes before the noun
one-thing.bodyMarkdown:
**yon** means “a” or “an” and comes before the noun.

- **yon liv** — a book
- **yon kaye** — a notebook
- **yon telefòn** — a phone

For now, focus on using the whole noun phrase naturally.

the-thing.title: The marker comes after the noun
the-thing.bodyMarkdown:
In Kreyòl, the definite marker comes **after** the noun.

Here are a few examples:

- **liv la** — the book
- **kaye a** — the notebook
- **telefòn nan** — the phone

You do not need to learn the full article-selection rule yet. Read and say these noun phrases as complete chunks.

more-than-one.title: Plural yo comes after the noun
more-than-one.bodyMarkdown:
For plural definite noun phrases, use **yo** after the noun.

- **liv yo** — the books
- **kaye yo** — the notebooks

The same **yo** works across these plural noun phrases.
